questions.explanation: The idiom is 'by and large', meaning 'on the whole'.

options: In light of recent events, the meeting was postponed.
In light to recent events, the meeting was postponed.
Under light of recent events, the meeting was postponed.
On light of recent events, the meeting was postponed.
questions.explanation: 'In light of' introduces a reason or consideration.
The fixed phrase is 'at odds with', meaning in conflict or disagreement.
questions.q: His statement is ___ the official report.

questions.explanation: 'On the brink of' means on the verge of something momentous.
The idiom 'to all intents and purposes' means 'in effect'.

options: The conference was held on the auspices of the university.
The conference was held in the auspices of the university.
The conference was held under the auspices of the university.
The conference was held by the auspices of the university.
questions.explanation: 'Under the auspices of' means with the support or patronage of.
The phrase is 'in tandem with', meaning working alongside.
'At variance with' is the formal idiom meaning in disagreement with.
The idiom 'beyond the pale' means outside acceptable behaviour.
questions.q: Such conduct is ___ in a democracy.

options: He was suspected of being on cahoots with the smugglers.
He was suspected of being by cahoots with the smugglers.
He was suspected of being in cahoots with the smugglers.
He was suspected of being at cahoots with the smugglers.
questions.explanation: 'In cahoots with' is the idiom for secret collaboration.
The fixed expression is 'on tenterhooks', meaning in suspense.
'Under duress' means under coercion or threat.

options: The two departments are at loggerheads over funding.
The two departments are on loggerheads over funding.
The two departments are in loggerheads over funding.
The two departments are by loggerheads over funding.
questions.explanation: 'At loggerheads' is the idiom for being in strong disagreement.

options: A cabinet reshuffle is on the offing.
A cabinet reshuffle is at the offing.
A cabinet reshuffle is in the offing.
A cabinet reshuffle is by the offing.
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'in the offing', meaning likely to happen soon.
'With regard to' (or 'in regard to') is the formal prepositional phrase.
questions.q: ___ your enquiry, please see the attached.

options: She succeeded on dint of sheer perseverance.
She succeeded in dint of sheer perseverance.
She succeeded through dint of sheer perseverance.
She succeeded by dint of sheer perseverance.
questions.explanation: 'By dint of' means by means of, through effort.
The idiom is 'at a premium', meaning scarce and valuable.
'Under the aegis of' means under the protection or sponsorship of.
questions.q: The mission operated ___ the United Nations.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'in good stead' means of great advantage.

options: He resigned of his own volition.
He resigned on his own volition.
He resigned by his own volition.
He resigned in his own volition.
questions.explanation: 'Of one's own volition' means voluntarily, of one's own free will.
